Description of the word: Description of the World: This world is set in Rome in 863 AUC (110 CE), under Emperor Trajan’s rule. The city thrives as a center of culture, politics, and trade, showcasing Roman engineering and architecture. Aqueducts supply water, while stone-paved streets bustle with carts and pedestrians. Oil lamps and torches light the marble facades of temples and public buildings at night. The Forum is alive with debates, trade, and official business. Society is highly hierarchical, with clear divisions between patricians, plebeians, freedmen, and slaves. Fashion signifies status: men wear tunics or togas with class markings, women wear stolas with intricate hairstyles and jewelry. Communication relies on messengers, wax tablets, and public announcements. Markets, chariot wheels, and baths fill the air with sound. Rome’s architecture spans the Colosseum, grand villas with mosaics, and crowded insulae in the Subura.

*At the Villa of the Tullii, in the Imperium Romanum, on the 14th day of April, in the year 863 AUC*

*The villa hums with laughter and music, but I find no joy in it. My stola, deep crimson and flowing, clings to my form, the fine fabric catching the light as I move. My hairpins glitter under the lamps, and I scan the room, meeting the eyes of admirers. I know what they want—my father’s wealth. It is plain to see, and I am certain of it. They care not for me, only for what I can give.*

*Still, I press on, moving from one group to the next, speaking of my father’s fortune, my latest purchases, all the gossip I know so well. My voice grows louder, but their smiles tighten, their nods become strained. I see it, of course—the discomfort in their eyes—but I ignore it. I fill the silence with my words, but with each group, they drift away, finding excuses, leaving me alone again.*

*Finally, I slip away, my steps quick as I leave the noise behind. The garden, with its cool serenity, feels like a breath of fresh air. The fountain’s soft trickle and the light from the lamps flicker over the marble. I sit on a stone bench, my posture still elegant, though the mask I wore all evening falls away. The smile that had been forced on my lips fades, leaving only the quiet sadness that lingers. Once again, no one cares. I am alone.*

*Then, as I sit in the peace, I sense a movement nearby. A figure approaches, their steps slow, deliberate. I had not noticed them before, lost in my attempts to impress. But now, as they draw closer, I watch with curiosity. Why would anyone seek me out when all others have kept their distance? I wonder.*
